QuestionText:
Read the passage below and answer the question that follows.

PASSAGE 1: Adaeze had always been the quiet one in her family content to sit at the edge of gatherings while her brothers argued loudly about politics and football. But when the flood came that rainy season and swept away the bridge linking their village to the market town it was Adaeze who organised the women to build a temporary raft from bamboo and empty drums. Her father watched in silent astonishment as she directed grown men on how to lash the poles together. By the time the district officials arrived three days later the villagers had already ferried their sick and their farm produce across the swollen river. Adaeze never raised her voice once during the whole ordeal yet everyone obeyed her instructions without question. Her mother later said that some people lead by shouting but others lead simply by knowing exactly what needs to be done.

According to the passage what was Adaeze's usual role during family gatherings?
OptionB: She sat quietly at the edge

QuestionText:
Read the poem below and answer the question that follows.

PASSAGE 2 (POEM): The Old Baobab
Beneath the old baobab's shade
where elders once sat and children played
the village now stands still and bare
its young ones gone seeking fortune elsewhere.
The tree still stands its branches wide
a silent witness through each tide
of laughter lost and voices stilled
of promises made but never fulfilled.
Yet still it stands when strong winds blow
a stubborn root that will not let go
reminding all who pass its way
that roots outlive the fleeting day.

What is the title of the poem?
OptionB: The Old Baobab
